free_tier.stated: Free, no published per-dataset or per-account cap. 'Is this service free to use? Yes!' A 6.4 TB dataset has been deposited (staged incrementally).

retention.stated: per-object-cap: none published; the real cap is a transient staging worker ('files are stored on a worker with relatively limited storage space'), so very large datasets must be uploaded in batches with ~24 h waits between snapshots. Retention: permanent, every version gets its own DOI; 36-month grace before forced public release

egress.terms: Free and anonymous. Objects live on Amazon S3 (`s3.amazonaws.com/openneuro.org`), public-read, ranged, CORS-open. No auth, no egress meter.

tooling: openneuro-cli (`openneuro upload`) + git-annex, and DataLad. Read side is plain anonymous S3 GET — any S3 client, rclone's s3 remote with no credentials, or plain curl.
chaining: Unlimited datasets, each a fresh S3 prefix under `openneuro.org/ds<ID>/`. Because the read side is unauthenticated S3, fetch volume never touches OpenNeuro's app tier.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published; the real cap is a transient staging worker ('files are stored on a worker with relatively limited storage space'), so very large datasets must be uploaded in batches with ~24 h waits between snapshots. Retention: permanent, every version gets its own DOI; 36-month grace before forced public release. Binding read limit is per-ip-shaping but weak.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Large uploads fail in the staging area and require batch-then-wait choreography; BIDS format is mandatory and undeface-d datasets get deleted after the fact.
